insights.title: Net room growth guidance moves to low end
insights.summary: Full-year 2026 net room growth was guided at 4.5% to 5% on the Q4 2025 call. On the Q2 2026 call management said growth is now more likely toward the low end of that range, citing Middle East construction delays and the usual 1% to 1.5% room deletions.
insights.uw_relevance: Unit growth drives fee growth in this asset-light model, so a slower path matters for fee forecasts. The shortfall is tied to the Middle East, which is also a source of RevPAR pressure.

evidence.snippet: For the full year 2026, net room growth is expected to accelerate up to 4.5% to 5%.
evidence.source_title: MARRIOTT INTERNATIONAL INC /MD/ earnings call 2025Q4 (quarter ended 2025-12-31)

evidence.snippet: Our full year 2026 net rooms growth is now more likely to be towards the low end of our previous 4.5% to 5% range, primarily due to construction delays in the Middle East
evidence.source_title: MARRIOTT INTERNATIONAL INC /MD/ earnings call 2026Q2 (quarter ended 2026-06-30)

insights.title: Middle East conflict emerges as guidance risk
insights.summary: The Q1 2026 call first framed the Middle East conflict as a guidance assumption, with a 100 to 125 basis point possible hit to full-year global RevPAR growth. On the Q2 2026 call Middle East RevPAR was reported down 43% in the quarter and the full-year impact was put at about 100 basis points.
insights.uw_relevance: The conflict is a new, event-driven exposure that affects RevPAR, IMF fees, and development timing. Management noted the Middle East is 3% of open rooms and 7% of pipeline rooms, so the exposure is concentrated.

evidence.snippet: Our guidance assumes the conflict in the Middle East could impact full year global RevPAR growth by 100 to 125 basis points.
evidence.source_title: MARRIOTT INTERNATIONAL INC /MD/ earnings call 2026Q1 (quarter ended 2026-03-31)

evidence.snippet: Middle East RevPAR declined 43% in the quarter, a bit better than prior expectations on better-than-expected domestic leisure demand.
evidence.source_title: MARRIOTT INTERNATIONAL INC /MD/ earnings call 2026Q2 (quarter ended 2026-06-30)

insights.title: Investment spend guidance raised across three calls
insights.summary: Expected 2026 investment spending rose from $1 billion to $1.1 billion on the Q4 2025 call to $1.25 billion to $1.35 billion on the Q2 2026 call. Contract acquisition costs, which were 35% to 40% of the total at the start, were guided to 40% to 45% by Q2.
insights.uw_relevance: Rising spend on contract acquisition (key money) and tech transformation raises capital deployed ahead of fee income. Management said it remains disciplined on key money per deal, which is a claim the calls did not quantify beyond comparisons to prior years.

evidence.snippet: The remaining 35% to 40% is expected investment in our contracts.

insights.title: Credit card royalty rate raised, deals renegotiated
insights.summary: On the Q4 2025 call management said it had increased the royalty rate on co-branded cards and guided co-branded card fees up around 35%. By the Q2 2026 call it announced new long-term U.S. agreements with JPMorgan Chase and American Express, at a royalty rate of 26%, and guided global card fees to the high 30% range.
insights.uw_relevance: A large share of the fee growth now depends on renegotiated card contracts whose full benefit builds over several quarters. Underwriters should note that the economics rest on third-party partner terms and on continued loyalty program engagement.

insights.title: Owner relations tone turns defensive
insights.summary: On the Q4 2025 call the CEO said the owner and franchise community was at a different stage of recovery and that Marriott was looking at every variable in owner returns. On the Q2 2026 call, asked about an owner letter, he declined to give an official response, calling it a matter between Marriott and its owners.
insights.uw_relevance: Owner friction in an asset-light model can affect development, fee terms and reputational exposure. Management described discussions as constructive and ongoing, but declined to address the letter directly.

followups.uw_relevance: Higher borrowing alongside negative equity increases the leverage exposure a D&O underwriter reviews.

followups.question: What is the nature, counterparties and scope of the $27 million property-related litigation accrual recorded in the 2026 second quarter?

metric_relevance.accruals_ratio: Accruals over total assets were -2.2% in FY2025 and -1.4% in FY2024, and -0.6% in FY2026 Q2. Negative accruals mean reported earnings are backed by cash, and the $27M property litigation accrual (K5) is the kind of charge to check against this line.
metric_relevance.adr: Average daily rate was $193.66 in FY2026 Q2, up from $187.70 in FY2026 Q1 and $183.71 in FY2025 Q3. Rate gains support fee revenue, but the Middle East RevPAR decline (K6) shows that rate growth is not uniform across regions.
metric_relevance.altman_z: The Altman Z-score rose each year from 2.54 in FY2021 to 3.66 in FY2024 and 3.75 in FY2025. This model signal partly offsets concerns about negative equity (K1) and rising debt (K3), but it is a model output rather than a credit rating.
metric_relevance.buyback_intensity: Buybacks were 1.46x net income in FY2026 Q2 and 2.25x in FY2025 Q4, with 1.27x for FY2025. Returning more than earnings while equity is negative is the pattern flagged in K1 and R2.
metric_relevance.buybacks: Share repurchases were $1.12B in FY2026 Q2, $3.30B in FY2025 and $3.76B in FY2024, and management expects over $4.5B of 2026 shareholder returns (R2). Repurchases continued while equity is negative, which draws the scrutiny described in K1.
metric_relevance.capex: Capital expenditures were $152M in FY2026 Q2 and $604M for FY2025, down from $750M in FY2024. Investment spend guidance rose to $1.25B to $1.35B (B3), and contract acquisition costs are a growing share of that, so capex alone understates the investment outlay.
metric_relevance.cash: Cash and equivalents were $462M at FY2026 Q2, against current liabilities of $7.90B and down from $1.39B in FY2021. Thin cash alongside negative working capital (K2) is why liquidity is a central D&O question.
metric_relevance.current_assets: Current assets rose to $4.23B at FY2026 Q2 from $3.58B at FY2025 year-end, but remain well below current liabilities of $7.90B. The gap between these two lines drives the 0.53x current ratio flagged in K2 and R5.
metric_relevance.current_liabilities: Current liabilities were $7.90B at FY2026 Q2, down from $8.52B in FY2026 Q1 and $8.40B at FY2025 year-end, and remain well above current assets of $4.23B. This obligation level is the core of the liquidity concern in K2 and R5.
metric_relevance.current_ratio: The current ratio was 0.53x at FY2026 Q2, up from 0.43x at FY2025 year-end and 0.40x at FY2024 year-end, and it has been below 1x in every period shown. Short-term obligations are not covered by current assets, so the company's ability to meet them depends on cash flow and refinancing (K2, R5).
metric_relevance.debt_due_1y: Debt due within one year was $1.21B in FY2025, down from $1.31B in FY2024 and up from $553M in FY2023. This near-term maturity load, set against cash of $358M at FY2025 year-end, is the refinancing need behind K3.
metric_relevance.debt_to_equity: Debt-to-equity is N/M from FY2023 through FY2026 Q2 because equity is negative, so leverage is judged on debt, interest coverage and cash flow instead. The last meaningful value was 17.72x in FY2022, before equity turned negative (K1).
metric_relevance.diluted_shares_growth_yoy: Diluted share count fell 4.1% in FY2025, 5.8% in FY2024 and 7.0% in FY2023, showing buybacks are shrinking the share base. The reduction is consistent with $3.30B of FY2025 repurchases (R2), which continue alongside negative equity.
metric_relevance.ebitda_computed: EBITDA was $1.45B in FY2026 Q2 and $4.74B for FY2025, but FY2025 Q4 and FY2024 Q4 are N/M, so the quarterly trend has gaps. With total debt at $16.91B (K3), EBITDA is the base for judging how much debt the company can carry.
metric_relevance.eps_surprise_pct: EPS surprise was 4.2% in FY2026 Q2 and 6.7% in FY2026 Q1, after -1.5% in FY2025 Q4 and -2.2% in FY2024 Q3. Earnings misses are a common trigger for share-price drops, so the recent beats reduce near-term pressure.
metric_relevance.equity: Stockholders' equity was -$4.53B at FY2026 Q2, negative in every period since FY2023 (-$682M) and down from $568M in FY2022. The deepening deficit while buybacks continue (K1, R2) is the central governance pressure point.
metric_relevance.free_cash_flow: Free cash flow was $796M in FY2026 Q2 and $2.61B for FY2025, but -$24M in FY2024 Q4. FY2025 buybacks of $3.30B exceeded this free cash flow, so the gap between cash generation and returns is the core funding question (K1, R2).
metric_relevance.goodwill_impairment: Goodwill impairment was $0.00 in each year from FY2021 to FY2025, so no goodwill write-off has been recorded. The separate $68M impairment charge in the 2026 second quarter (R10) is the impairment event to examine.
metric_relevance.goodwill_to_equity: Goodwill to equity is N/M from FY2023 to FY2025 because equity is negative, after 15.62x in FY2022 and 6.42x in FY2021. Goodwill is no longer a meaningful measure of equity cushion, so balance-sheet judgment relies on debt and liquidity instead.
metric_relevance.gross_fee_revenue: Gross fee revenues were $1.58B in FY2026 Q2 and $5.44B in FY2025, up from $4.82B in FY2023. Fee income is the franchise and management base, and the card royalty change and new deal terms bear directly on it (K10, B4).
metric_relevance.insider_net_sales: Net insider open-market sales were $34M in FY2026 Q1, $26M in FY2025 Q4 and $3M in FY2026 Q2. Sales recurring across periods during buybacks and negative equity (K9, R3) are the pattern the D&O review focuses on.
metric_relevance.interest_coverage: Interest coverage was 5.56x at FY2026 Q2 after a low of 3.74x in FY2025 Q4, and was 5.12x for FY2025 against 8.59x in FY2022. The downward trend as interest expense climbs is the swing flagged in K3.
metric_relevance.interest_expense: Interest expense was $221M in FY2026 Q2, up from $203M in FY2025 Q2, and $809M for FY2025 against $403M in FY2022. Management ties the increase to Senior Notes issuance (R12), which is adding cost as debt rises (K3).
metric_relevance.long_term_debt: Long-term debt rose to $16.45B at FY2026 Q2 from $14.99B at FY2025 year-end and $9.38B in FY2022. Management attributes the rise to Senior Notes issuance net of maturities (R12), so the terms and purpose of new issuance drive the D&O question.
metric_relevance.market_cap: Market capitalization was $96.64B at FY2026 Q2, up from $82.21B at FY2025 year-end. Its large gap to negative book equity of -$4.53B means investors are valuing the franchise, not the balance sheet, so share-price drops would carry significant claim exposure.
metric_relevance.max_drawdown_52w: The 52-week max drawdown was -12.6% at FY2026 Q2, narrowed from -30.5% at FY2025 year-end. A drawdown of that depth is the kind of price decline that can prompt securities claims if disclosures are later challenged.
metric_relevance.near_term_debt_coverage: Debt due in one year relative to cash plus operating cash flow was 0.34x in FY2025, down from 0.42x in FY2024 and up from 0.16x in FY2023. A value below 1x means near-term maturities are less than cash plus operating cash flow, but the trend has moved within a wide band (K3).
metric_relevance.net_fee_revenue: Net fee revenues were $1.55B in FY2026 Q2 and $5.30B in FY2025, against $5.07B in FY2024. This net line is exposed to the Middle East RevPAR decline (K6) and the card deal terms (K10), and the $100M to $125M fee range by 2028 depends on those terms (R11).
metric_relevance.net_income: Net income was $766M in FY2026 Q2 and $648M in FY2026 Q1, against $2.60B for FY2025 and $3.08B for FY2023. Earnings are the denominator for buyback intensity (1.46x in FY2026 Q2, K1), and the $68M impairment in the same quarter (R10) bears on the reported figure.
metric_relevance.occupancy: Occupancy was 71.6% in FY2026 Q2, after 65.6% in FY2026 Q1 and 67.4% in FY2025 Q4. Occupancy and rate together drive RevPAR, and the Middle East decline of 43% (K6) is the main operating risk to these figures.
metric_relevance.officer_sell_pct: Officers sold 31.4% of holdings in FY2026 Q1 and 14.2% in FY2026 Q2, after 30.5% in FY2025 Q1 and 0.0% in FY2025 Q3. Large officer disposals in quarters when the company was repurchasing shares are the scrutiny point in K9 and R3.
metric_relevance.operating_cash_flow: Operating cash flow was $948M in FY2026 Q2 and $3.21B for FY2025, but only $318M in FY2024 Q4, so quarterly cash generation is uneven. It is the main source for shareholder returns (over $4.5B expected for 2026, R2), so its durability bears on the funding question.
metric_relevance.operating_income: Operating income was $1.23B in FY2026 Q2, up from $777M in FY2025 Q4, and $4.14B for FY2025 against $3.77B for FY2024. The $68M impairment charge was booked in depreciation, amortization and other expense in Q2 2026 (R10), so the operating line carries that write-down.
metric_relevance.receivables_days: Days sales outstanding were 41 days in FY2025 and FY2024, down from 52 days in FY2021. Collections are steady, so receivables do not add to the liquidity concern.
metric_relevance.revenue: Total revenue was $7.07B in FY2026 Q2 and $26.19B in FY2025, but dipped to $6.65B in FY2026 Q1 after $6.69B in FY2025 Q4. The Q2 level is the base for the co-brand card fee outlook (K10), while Middle East RevPAR weakness (K6) is the main threat to the top line.
metric_relevance.revenue_growth_qoq: Sequential growth swung from -3.8% in FY2025 Q3 to 6.3% in FY2026 Q2, after -0.5% in FY2026 Q1, so quarter-to-quarter moves are volatile. The Q2 2026 rebound coincides with the new card agreements (K10), which makes the driver of that jump worth checking.
metric_relevance.revenue_growth_yoy: Year-over-year growth was 4.8% in FY2026 Q2 and 6.2% in FY2026 Q1, below 14.2% in FY2023, and FY2025 full year was 4.3%. Management ties Q2 growth partly to new card deals (K10), while the Middle East RevPAR drop of 43% (K6) could slow growth further.
metric_relevance.revpar: RevPAR was $138.74 in FY2026 Q2, up from $123.09 in FY2026 Q1, but Middle East RevPAR fell 43% in the quarter (K6). The full-year global RevPAR impact is now about 100 basis points (R9), and the Middle East is 3% of open rooms.
metric_relevance.sbc_to_revenue: Stock compensation was 0.9% of revenue in each year from FY2022 to FY2025, down from 1.3% in FY2021. Pay levels are steady, so equity compensation is not the source of the current governance questions.
metric_relevance.total_debt: Total debt reached $16.91B at FY2026 Q2, up from $16.20B at FY2025 year-end and $10.06B in FY2022. Debt has grown while stockholders' equity is negative, which is the leverage concern in K3 and R12.
metric_relevance.volatility_90d: The 90-day share price volatility was 26.5% at FY2026 Q2 and 30.0% at FY2026 Q1, and has ranged between 21.7% and 37.7% across the quarters shown. Elevated volatility around disclosures on the CFO change (K8) and owner disagreements (K7) raises stock-price risk.
metric_relevance.working_capital: Working capital was -$3.68B at FY2026 Q2, improved from -$4.81B at FY2025 year-end but still deeply negative and -$2.78B in FY2021. The shortfall is the basis of the liquidity warning in K2 and R5, and the question is whether operating cash flow covers it.
